chunks: And from him, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Murāzim, who said:
Ismāʿīl ibn Jābir asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام and said: May Allah set you right, I have many supererogatory prayers due upon me, so what should I do?
So he said: “Make them up.” He said to him: They are more than that. He said: “Make them up.” I said: I cannot enumerate them. He said: “Estimate them to the best of your judgment.”

Murāzim said: I had been ill for four months during which I did not perform supererogatory prayers, so I said to him: May Allah set you right, or may I be made your ransom, I was ill for four months and did not perform any supererogatory prayer. He said: “There is no making up due upon you. Indeed, the sick person is not like the healthy person. Everything over which Allah has overcome him, then Allah is more entitled to excuse him in it.”

key_terms.اقْضِهَا: make them up as missed devotional acts
key_terms.الْعُذْرِ: legal excuse or exemption due to inability
key_terms.الْمَرِيضَ: the sick person who is under a legal excuse
key_terms.تَوَخَّ: estimate and act according to best judgment
key_terms.قَضَاءٌ: make-up performance of a missed act of worship
key_terms.لَا أُحْصِيهَا: I cannot count or enumerate them precisely
key_terms.نَوَافِلَ: supererogatory prayers beyond the obligatory salat

ai.seo_question: Does a sick person have to make up missed nawafil, and what if the number of missed prayers is unknown?
ai.summary: This hadith states that missed nawafil are to be made up, and if their number is unknown, one should estimate them as best as possible. It also clarifies that nawafil missed due to illness do not require qada', because the sick person is excused for what was beyond his ability.
